sections.title: The letters ir
paragraphs: The letters ir sound like /ɜːr/. You hear this sound in (bird) /bɜːrd/, which means a feathered animal that flies. These letters make three different sounds in English. Each sound depends on the word stress and the letters that come next.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: For the first sound, keep your tongue in the middle of the mouth. Curl the tip back slightly and relax your lips. For the second sound, make a short, weak vowel with the tongue relaxed. For the third sound, open your mouth wide, glide to a close vowel, and finish in the middle. Place your hand on your throat to feel your voice shake.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: The letters ir make their main sound in a stressed syllable. You hear this sound in (shirt) /ʃɜːrt/. In an unstressed syllable, they make a short, weak sound, as in (elixir) /ɪ.lɪk.sər/. Before a silent e, they make a long glide, as in (wire) /waɪ.ər/. They also make that glide before another vowel, as in (fire) /faɪ.ər/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not read these letters as two separate sounds. Never roll your tongue tip on the upper teeth. Keep the lips relaxed instead of pushing them out like an o sound. Do not say the clear vowel of see. Hold the sound steady in words like (bird) /bɜːrd/.
